title: Chapter test: Packages, Crates and Modules
summary: Ten questions on crates, modules, privacy, paths and use. You need 70% to pass; you can retry and your best score is kept.

questions.q: How many library crates can one package contain?
questions.explanation: Any number of binaries, at most one library.

questions.q: Where does Cargo expect an extra binary called `migrate`?
options: It must be declared in `Cargo.toml` with a path
questions.explanation: Each file in `src/bin/` is a binary crate.
`a` is a sibling of `main`, so it may be named; `b` is `pub`; but `hidden` is private to `b`.

questions.q: Code in `mod kitchen` (a child of the crate root) wants to call `serve()` defined at the crate root. Which path works?
questions.explanation: `super` is the parent module, here the crate root. `crate::serve()` would also work.

questions.q: Given `pub struct Config { pub name: String, secret: String }` in module `settings`, which can code outside `settings` do?
options: Call a `pub fn new` that `settings` provides
questions.explanation: Private fields block both access and struct literals from outside.

questions.q: To make an enum's variants usable outside its module, each variant must be marked `pub`.
questions.explanation: A `pub enum` makes all variants public.

questions.q: Which `use` follows the convention for a type?
A module declares `use crate::utils::helper;`. Can a child module of it call `helper()` without its own `use`?
options: No, a `use` only applies to the scope where it is written

questions.q: The automatically imported list of common items such as `Vec` and `Option` is called the standard ______.
`src/lib.rs` has `mod net;` and `src/net.rs` has `pub mod tcp;`. Where is `tcp`'s code?
questions.explanation: A child module's file sits in a folder named after its parent.
